items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: Benny had a guitarist with him, a very good guitarist from Cleveland by the name of Willie Lewis... Benny asked me to come with the band.

ctx.x: And I went to New York, and Nat Cole -- I hadn't seen Nat in years because when I went to New York he went to California so I didn't see him, but I had heard about what he was doing. But any way this was -- now, this had to be in 1941, around 1941, so at the Kelly's Stables Nat Cole was appearing, and also Benny Carter's band. So I went in and I heard Nat's group, and it was just beautiful. I just loved it, you know, and it -- I was also glad to see him, and surprised to hear him sing, you know, because Nat and I…

Nat was a tremendous pianist, he was a genius on this piano. But I never knew that Nat could sing, you know. When I heard him sing it was just something, and I would -- and Benny's band was good, and it was just good to get out of Mississippi. And Benny had a guitarist with him, a very good guitarist from Cleveland by the name of Willie Lewis. He was blues oriented. That was his background.

But any way, they had some argument or something, and I don't know whether Benny fired him that night or he quit, but any way Benny asked me to come with the band. So I got on the phone and called Fletcher in Chicago and told Fletcher that I wanted to stay, and Fletcher begged me to come back and I'd say Fletcher, you just can't do this to me, I'm so tired of the road and so and so and so and so. But if you insist. He said, well, John, if you just want to stay there, okay.
